newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Worldwide says sales accelerating.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Worldwide says sales accelerating.

text.p: Johnson Worldwide Associates Inc said Monday it has seen sales start to pick up after posting a nine percent decline in the fiscal 1997 first quarter ended December 27.

"The nine percent decrease in first quarter sales resulted from a continuation of the disappointing retail environment, exaggerating what is typically a light, off-season quarter for fishing, camping, and diving products," R.C. Whitaker, chief executive officer, said in a news release. "We now are seeing sales orders begin to accelerate as customers anticipate the arrival of warmer weather."
Meanwhile, the sporting goods products maker said it is having some success containing costs.

"Operating expenses of $21.3 million reflect a 9 percent reduction from one year ago," Whitaker said. "Irrespective of market cycles, we are committed to making cost management an integral part of our ongoing operating philosophy."
Earlier, the company reported a loss of $3.9 million, or $0.48 a sahre for the first quarter, compared to a loss of $2.8 million, or $0.34 a share a year ago.
